PAPERS.short: Zhu source-specific PM2.5 atrial fibrillation Medicare cohort 2026
PAPERS.title: Source-Specific PM2.5 Exposure and Atrial Fibrillation Risk in U.S. Older Adults: A Nationwide Cohort Study
PAPERS.pm: Source-apportioned PM2.5 (Multilinear Engine on CSN/IMPROVE speciation; IDW to ZIP code, 100 km)
PAPERS.n: 26.3 million Medicare beneficiaries, 2000-2019, 171.6 M person-years, 4.44 M incident AF. Per IQR of source-specific PM2.5: secondary sulfate HR 1.056 (1.053-1.058), heavy oil/coal combustion 1.048 (1.046-1.050), secondary nitrate 1.032 (1.030-1.034), vehicle 1.029 (1.028-1.030); biomass burning and dust modest, SOA null overall but positive in the West. Limitation: source profiles come from sparse speciation monitors interpolated by inverse distance over 100 km, so source contrasts are largely regional contrasts; sulfate and nitrate fields are smooth and the per-IQR scaling differs by source, so 'sulfate is most toxic' is not a per-microgram statement. Claims-based AF under-ascertains paroxysmal AF. Relevance: high - speciation, not mass, is what optical LCS cannot give; source-resolved risk raises the value of co-located filter or ACSM nodes.

PAPERS.short: Lin air pollution cervical cancer recurrence mortality Fudan cohort 2026
PAPERS.title: Long-Term Exposure to Ambient Air Pollution and Cervical Cancer Outcomes in Chinese Women: A Prospective Study on Recurrence and Mortality Risks
PAPERS.pm: Residential PM2.5 and PM10 from high-resolution spatiotemporal models (post-surgery)
PAPERS.endpoint: Cervical cancer recurrence and all-cause death
PAPERS.n: 3,758 women with primary cervical cancer (2019-2022), median follow-up ~3 y; 217 recurrences, 113 deaths. Per IQR PM2.5: recurrence SHR 1.93 (1.40-2.66, Fine-Gray), death HR 2.55 (1.78-3.67); PM10 SHR 1.65 (1.13-2.42) and HR 2.21 (1.38-3.54); NO2 and SO2 also positive, O3 null. Limitation: hazard ratios near 2-2.5 per IQR from 113 deaths are implausibly large for a residential long-term contrast and point to confounding by referral geography - patients from outside Shanghai (higher PM) likely differ in stage, HPV management and follow-up intensity; single-centre, short follow-up, no adjustment for distance to the hospital reported in the abstract. Relevance: low - model-based residential exposure, no sensing implication.

PAPERS.short: Li size-specific PM lung function China Pulmonary Health Study 2026
PAPERS.title: Associations between Size-Specific Particulate Matter and Lung Function: Results from the China Pulmonary Health Study
PAPERS.pm: Long-term PM1, PM1-2.5, PM2.5, PM2.5-10, PM10 (per IQR)
PAPERS.endpoint: Spirometry: FEV1, FVC, FEV1/FVC, FEF75, FEF25-75
PAPERS.n: 50,991 adults >=20 y from the China Pulmonary Health Study; multivariable linear models on long-term size-resolved PM. Per IQR PM1: FEV1 -36.84 mL (-45.91 to -27.76), FVC -34.63 mL (-45.48 to -23.79); large-airway decrements grew as particle size fell, whereas the coarse fraction PM2.5-10 gave the largest small-airway (FEF75, FEF25-75) decrements. Limitation: size fractions are derived from correlated modelled surfaces (PM1 and PM2.5 share most of their mass), and the abstract reports no multi-fraction model, so 'size-specific' ranking may reflect differential exposure-model error rather than biology; cross-sectional. Relevance: high - optical LCS report PM1 and coarse bins natively, and this is evidence that those channels carry distinct health signal worth calibrating, not discarding.

PAPERS.title: The association of particulate matter 2.5 exposure with frailty trajectories in middle-aged and older Chinese adults and the potential modification by lifestyle and socioeconomic status
PAPERS.n: 10,659 CHARLS participants; deficit-accumulation frailty index, three GBTM trajectories (stable low 64%, increasing to frailty 29%, continuously worsening 7%). Per 10 ug/m3 PM2.5, odds of the two adverse trajectories rose 15.2% and 12.3% (ordered logistic; no CIs in the abstract). Higher SES attenuated the association (RERI -0.067); unhealthy sleep duration amplified it (RERI 0.163). Limitation: GBTM classes are model artefacts with posterior misclassification carried into a second-stage regression without uncertainty propagation; CHARLS addresses are coarse (city/county), so exposure contrast is mostly between regions with different healthcare and diet. Relevance: low - regional satellite exposure, no sensing implication.

PAPERS.short: Sun long-term air pollution lipid profiles Shanxi repeated measures 2026
PAPERS.title: Long-term exposure to ambient air pollution and lipid profiles: a longitudinal study in a heavily industrialized region of northern China
PAPERS.n: Repeated-measures study of 9,040 adults with 19,113 lipid measurements from a health-screening programme, 2019-2023. Per 10 ug/m3 PM2.5: TG +1.85%, TC +1.70%, LDL-C +1.81%, HDL-C -1.55% (linear mixed models); PM10, NO2, SO2 and O3 in the same direction, CO weaker; age modified the HDL-C association after FDR correction. Limitation: a health-screening population self-selects; CHAP is itself trained on the sparse Shanxi monitor network that underrepresents coal-industry hotspots, and with five correlated pollutants the 'PM2.5 most pronounced' ranking is not identified from single-pollutant models. Lipids are sensitive to fasting status, not mentioned. Relevance: moderate - industrial-region exposure surfaces are where LCS densification would most change CHAP errors.

PAPERS.short: Mai population-weighted PM2.5 O3 China 2015-2024 preprint 2026
PAPERS.title: Population Weighted Ambient PM2.5 and O3 Concentrations in China from 2015 to 2024
PAPERS.pm: Annual ~1 km CHAP PM2.5 and O3 weighted by WorldPop
PAPERS.n: Ecological geospatial analysis of annual ~1 km CHAP PM2.5/O3 rasters matched to WorldPop counts, 2015-2024. Population-weighted PM2.5 fell from 53.06 to 31.25 ug/m3 (-41.1%) while population-weighted O3 rose from 77.06 to 96.75 ug/m3 (+25.6%); the population-weighted minus geographic gap narrowed for PM2.5 (5.77 to 2.43) and widened for O3 (1.01 to 2.72). 97.4% of 0.2-degree blocks show falling PM2.5 with rising O3 at a 0.5 ug/m3/y threshold. Limitation: purely descriptive and inherits CHAP's ML smoothing; no uncertainty on the weighted means; preprint, not peer reviewed. Relevance: moderate - the narrowing urban-rural PM2.5 gap shifts LCS value toward peri-urban and rural siting.

PAPERS.title: IL-17 Signaling Pathway: A Potential Signaling Pathway Mediating Neuroinflammation Induced by PM2.5
PAPERS.pm: Collected PM2.5 suspension (dose not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.n: BV2 microglia exposed to PM2.5 lost viability and raised inflammatory cytokines; microarray DEGs enriched for inflammatory GO terms and the KEGG IL-17 pathway with downstream NF-kB and MAPK. An anti-IL-17A antibody reversed cytokine release, microglial activation and behavioural deficits (implying an in vivo arm). Limitation: the abstract gives no PM2.5 source, composition or dose, so environmental relevance cannot be judged; BV2 is an immortalised murine line with an exaggerated inflammatory phenotype, and IL-17 is usually T-cell/gamma-delta derived, so microglial IL-17 signalling needs cell-type attribution. Relevance: low - mechanistic only.

PAPERS.short: Ge preconception folic acid air pollution birthweight 2026
PAPERS.title: Preconception Folic Acid Supplementation Associated with Attenuated Effects of Air Pollution on Birthweight Outcomes
PAPERS.pm: Ambient air pollution (metrics not stated in record)
PAPERS.geo: China (inferred from author group; not stated in record)
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Ge, Zhang, Liao ... Berhane, Bai et al.); no abstract retrievable from PubMed, Europe PMC, Crossref or Semantic Scholar at harvest. The title claims effect modification of the air pollution-birthweight association by preconception folic acid use. Pollutants, cohort, n and effect sizes cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; supplement use is self-reported and strongly socially patterned, so 'attenuation' by folate is exposed to confounding by SES and antenatal-care quality unless handled explicitly. Relevance: low - no sensing content evident.

PAPERS.short: Pyae Tin Saw portable PM2.5 cross-site prediction fixed station 2026
PAPERS.title: Short-term PM2.5 data continuity: Cross-site prediction of portable measurements using a nearby fixed monitoring station
PAPERS.pm: Portable PM2.5 monitor vs nearby fixed-station PM2.5
PAPERS.geo: Thailand (inferred from author affiliation; not stated in record)
PAPERS.endpoint: Cross-site prediction / gap-filling of portable PM2.5
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Pyae Tin Saw, Kallawicha); day-0 Elsevier deposit with no abstract anywhere at harvest. The title describes predicting short-term portable PM2.5 records from a nearby fixed monitoring station to maintain data continuity. Sensor model, distance, n, and skill metrics cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; cross-site transfer functions are typically valid only within the regional-background regime and fail for local sources, which is exactly when portable data matter. Relevance: high - gap-filling an LCS or portable record against a regulatory anchor is a core network-operations problem.

PAPERS.short: Tripathi satellite-reanalysis sulfate aerosol India ground measurements 2026
PAPERS.title: Improving Satellite-Reanalysis Sulfate Aerosol Estimates over India Using Ground Measurements
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Tripathi, Sahu, Sharma, Gupta); no abstract indexed at harvest. The title indicates ground measurements used to correct satellite-reanalysis (likely MERRA-2/CAMS-type) sulfate aerosol over India. Data sources, method and skill cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; Indian speciation networks are sparse and urban-biased, so any correction trained on them risks transferring urban bias to rural cells. Relevance: moderate - component-resolved surfaces are the complement LCS mass networks lack; pairs with the sulfate-dominant AF signal in today's Medicare cohort.

PAPERS.short: Dayanandana CMIP6 dust optical depth MENA evaluation 2026
PAPERS.title: Evaluation of Dust Optical Depth in CMIP6 Simulations over the Middle East-North Africa Region
PAPERS.pm: Dust optical depth (CMIP6 models vs observations)
PAPERS.endpoint: Model skill for dust optical depth
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Dayanandana, Parottil, Abbas, Al-Harrasi et al.); no abstract at harvest. Evaluates CMIP6 dust optical depth over MENA, presumably against MODIS/MERRA-2 DOD. Models, metrics and biases cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; column optical depth maps to surface PM10 only through assumed vertical profiles and size distributions, so climate-model DOD skill says little about surface exposure. Relevance: low-moderate - MENA dust is where optical LCS mass error from coarse particles is largest.

PAPERS.short: Du Air Health Index acute myocardial infarction 325 cities 2026
PAPERS.title: Establishing an Air Health Index for Predicting the Risk of Acute Myocardial Infarction Onset Associated with Air Pollution and Ambient Temperature
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5 (with NO2, O3, temperature) from high-resolution surfaces
PAPERS.endpoint: AMI onset; composite Air Health Index (0-10+)
PAPERS.n: 1,207,625 AMI cases across 325 Chinese cities; excess risks from PM2.5, NO2, O3 and temperature aggregated into a normalised AHI. Per IQR, AHI associated with +5.97% (5.32-6.63%) AMI incidence vs +3.33% (2.93-3.72%) for AQHI and +2.04% (1.73-2.35%) for AQI; near-linear, no threshold; validated on an independent external dataset; 8,534 per 100,000 AMI cases attributed. Limitation: the index is fitted to the same outcome it is scored on, so in-sample superiority over AQI/AQHI is expected; IQR-scaled comparisons across indices with different distributions are not like-for-like, and 'attributable' fractions for a composite that includes temperature mix avoidable and non-avoidable risk. Relevance: high - an outcome-weighted index is a natural output layer for real-time LCS networks, provided the PM2.5 input is calibrated.

PAPERS.short: Zhang respirable magnetite emissions coal-fired power China 2026
PAPERS.title: Emissions of Respirable Magnetite from the Coal-Fired Power Sector in China: Spatial Inequalities and Mitigation Pathways
PAPERS.endpoint: Annual magnetite emission and mitigation scenarios
PAPERS.n: Multifactor emission model for respirable magnetite from Chinese coal-fired power: 2,828.7 (2,307.1-3,371.4) t/y, spatially concentrated by tiered emission standards. Guizhou and Sichuan supply 4% of coal power but tightening their standards alone would cut >31% of national magnetite emissions. Limitation: emission factors for magnetite specifically (as opposed to total PM or Fe) rest on few stack measurements, and the uncertainty interval looks narrow for a species-level inventory; health relevance is asserted from brain-magnetite literature rather than exposure-response data. Relevance: moderate - magnetite is invisible to optical LCS mass; magnetic or filter-based speciation would be needed to verify hotspots.

PAPERS.short: Ghaffarpasand Pope vehicle remote sensing real-world emissions high emitters 2026
PAPERS.title: Emerging Evidence on Real-World Exhaust Emissions and High Emitting Vehicles from Remote Sensing Observations
PAPERS.pm: On-road remote sensing of exhaust (pollutants not stated in record)
PAPERS.endpoint: Real-world exhaust emission factors; high-emitter identification
PAPERS.n: Title and authors only (Ghaffarpasand, Pope); no abstract at harvest. Appears to synthesise vehicle emission remote-sensing (VERSS) evidence on real-world exhaust and high emitters. Whether PM/smoke opacity or only NOx/CO/HC is covered cannot be stated. Limitation: unverifiable beyond the title; VERSS PM is inferred from UV opacity with large per-pass uncertainty, and single-pass snapshots overweight hot-running conditions. Relevance: moderate - high-emitter fractions explain the kerbside spikes roadside LCS record but cannot attribute.

PAPERS.short: Idowu medical waste incinerator airborne heavy metals Monte Carlo Nigeria 2026
PAPERS.title: Monte Carlo-Based Probabilistic Health Risk Assessment of Airborne Heavy Metals from a Medical Waste Incinerator in Southwestern Nigeria
PAPERS.pm: PM-bound heavy metals (passive glass-slide deposition samplers)
PAPERS.n: Particulate matter collected on passive glass slides around a medical-waste incinerator for two months; ten metals analysed, converted to airborne concentrations, and propagated through 10,000 Monte Carlo draws. Median HQ ~400, 95th percentile 850; exceedance probability near 100%; ILCR above benchmarks. Limitation: passive deposition slides measure settled mass, not airborne concentration - the conversion to C_air requires an assumed deposition velocity that dominates the result, and an HQ of 400 almost certainly reflects that conversion rather than real inhalation dose. Preprint. Relevance: moderate as a cautionary example - fence-line LCS or low-volume samplers would have given a defensible air concentration.

PAPERS.short: Jiang air pollution meteorology hand foot mouth disease Shenzhen DLNM 2026
PAPERS.title: Ambient air pollution and meteorological factors associated with hand, foot, and mouth disease risk in Shenzhen, China: a time-series study
PAPERS.pm: Daily city-wide PM2.5 and PM10 (fixed monitors)
PAPERS.n: Shenzhen daily HFMD counts 2013-2022 with six pollutants and meteorology in DLNMs, including pre/post EV71 vaccine and COVID-19 periods. PM2.5 and PM10 showed risk peaks at low concentrations and 'protective' effects at extreme highs; SO2 and CO raised cumulative risk at extremes; temperature showed a dual-peak pattern and high humidity raised risk. No effect sizes with CIs in the abstract. Limitation: HFMD is a contact-transmitted enteroviral disease with strong seasonality driven by school terms; non-monotone, sign-flipping PM curves are the signature of residual seasonal confounding and DLNM over-flexibility, not biology. Relevance: low.

PAPERS.short: Jiang PLA melt-blown nonwoven filtration durability humidity airflow 2026
PAPERS.title: Service Durability of PLA Melt-Blown Nonwovens: Roles of Humidity and Airflow Velocity in Degradation and Filtration Performance
PAPERS.pm: Filtration of particulate matter by PLA melt-blown media
PAPERS.endpoint: Fibre degradation kinetics, pressure drop, filtration efficiency
PAPERS.n: Full-factorial service-condition study (humidity, airflow velocity, PM loading, natural microbes) on PLA melt-blown filter media. Degradation stays early-stage, first-order, k up to 3.88e-2 /h, surface-erosion dominated. Humidity drives degradation (90% of short-term water-contact-angle variance; 77% of yield-strength and 91% of pressure-drop variance long-term); airflow velocity governs dynamic filtration via particle-media contact. Limitation: the abstract gives no filtration efficiency numbers by particle size, so it is unclear whether MPPS performance falls within a realistic mask or HVAC service life. Relevance: low - mitigation materials; humid-climate filter life matters for purifier intervention trials.

PAPERS.short: Alquwayi respirable crystalline silica occupational exposure Saudi Arabia review 2026
PAPERS.title: Potential risk of occupational exposure to respirable crystalline silica in Saudi Arabia: a comprehensive review of the current status and future challenges
PAPERS.endpoint: Occupational RCS exposure potential; silicosis surveillance gaps
PAPERS.n: Single-author review integrating literature, labour and mining statistics, mineralogy and regulation through a 'silica hazard triangle' (workforce, materials, activities). Concludes that mining, construction, cement, glass, engineered stone and photovoltaic manufacturing expansion plus arid-climate dust raise RCS exposure potential, while measured exposure, epidemiology and surveillance data are scarce. Limitation: no new measurements and no quantitative exposure estimates - the conclusion is an inference from sector size, not from data. Relevance: low-moderate - optical LCS cannot speciate silica, so RCS monitoring needs gravimetric/FTIR sampling regardless.
